clue.text: Electrician put on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside the letters standing for the vessel

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for the vessel one goes on board
to put a car somewhere is to park it

explanation.surface: Someone hires an electrician and installs them on the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention for going inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is a long-standing nickname for an electrician, and for a ship's radio operator.

clue.text: Horse in handicap, in touch

indicators.note: the first 'in' says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning their breaks

explanation.surface: A racehorse running in a handicap race is still in touch with the leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a horse with patchy piebald or skewbald markings.

clue.text: Listens during actual dummy run

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: actual means real
listens means hears

explanation.surface: Someone pays attention during a genuine practice run.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance before the real thing is a trial or dummy run.

clue.text: Fruit, no end, for ruler

indicators.note: the fruit word loses its final letter

parts.note: a sultana is a dried grape, a fruit

explanation.surface: A cheeky order: a piece of fruit with no end is fit for a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is a Muslim sovereign, a monarch ruling a sultanate.

clue.text: Engineers track access

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
a racecourse is a track

explanation.surface: Army engineers are building a track to give access to a site.
explanation.definitionFit: Having access to help or a remedy is having recourse to it; both mean a source to turn to.

clue.text: Rebels turn on sign

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a revolution is one full turn
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Rebels round on a placard or sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolutionaries are insurgents who rise up against a government, so they are rebels.

clue.text: Copper left — trial date coming up, getting close

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a court case is a trial

explanation.surface: A police officer has gone, the trial date is approaching and the verdict is getting close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives the metal's symbol; 'coming up' turns CASED into DESAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A close in British usage is a short dead-end residential street.

clue.text: Relative having soiled article removed

indicators.note: the article is taken out of the word for soiled

parts.note: soiled means unclean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A family member has had a dirty item taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family relation.

clue.text: Suspect something's wrong — let alarms off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone senses trouble and sets the alarms going.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sense foul play or suspect that something is amiss.

clue.text: Truthful in flat

explanation.surface: Someone is honest in their home, a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both honest and dead horizontal, as a spirit level shows.

clue.text: Gang from Cheshire town on the radio

indicators.note: words heard over the radio are spoken, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A gang from a Cheshire town features in a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working together, informally a gang.

clue.text: No thanks required by count, last off, so don't mention it

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: the final letter of the count word is dropped

parts.note: a tally is a count

explanation.surface: A count turns down gratitude, so the polite reply is to say nothing of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite set replies to someone who has just thanked you.

clue.text: Equally calm, lake close to city

parts.note: even-tempered means calm, even

indicators.note: close here means the end, so the last letter of city is taken

explanation.surface: A placid lake lies near a city.
explanation.definitionFit: To share evenly is to share in equal parts.

clue.text: Prejudice shown by British international — when?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A British international player is accused of prejudice, and someone asks when.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a one-sided inclination or partiality, much the same as prejudice.

clue.text: One name put forward beforehand

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to put forward an idea or a sum of money is to advance it

explanation.surface: One candidate's name was nominated ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ahead of time or earlier, a set synonym.

clue.text: Collaboration from me at sporting function

indicators.note: sporting here means playing around with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to work is to function

explanation.surface: Someone credits group effort for their success at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' looks like it describes the function, but it rearranges ME AT into TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Teamwork is people working together towards a shared aim, which is collaboration.

clue.text: How things stand with second wife wearing two hats?

indicators.note: being worn means being inside a garment, so one piece goes between the others
two signals the hat word appears twice

parts.note: a single hat is taken, then doubled

explanation.surface: A man asks how matters stand now that his second wife wears two hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two hats' doubles HAT, and SW sits between the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing what's what means knowing the true state of affairs.

clue.text: Piece of equipment that could make mum more embarrassed

parts.note: mum as in 'keep mum' means silent, which is the call sh
someone more embarrassed blushes, going redder

explanation.surface: A gadget that could make one's mother even more embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means silent, hence SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shredder is an office machine that cuts paper into strips, an item of equipment.

clue.text: Everyone taken in by most of band's blatant publicity

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: the final letter of the band word is dropped

parts.note: a hoop is a band or ring

explanation.surface: A whole crowd is fooled by a group's brash promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is not a link but the letters BY, which hold ALL; 'band' is a ring, not a music group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is loud, extravagant advertising or fuss.

clue.text: Stake in Victorian tearoom

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone holds a stake in an old-fashioned tearoom.
explanation.definitionFit: The ante is the stake each poker player puts up before the deal.

clue.text: Under pressure, ready for a change, said Grace?

indicators.note: in a down clue this word places the pressure letter as the top piece, above what follows

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

indicators.note: a change of order means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone under strain, eager for something different, gives thanks before a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a name but is the prayer said before meals; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying grace means offering a short prayer, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: A part of poem's hostile

parts.note: a verse is a stanza, part of a poem

explanation.surface: A section of a poem expresses hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed or ill-disposed towards it.

clue.text: One in eight perhaps bank on Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a bank of seats or keys is a row
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone puts money on the Queen being one of eight.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing boat with eight oarsmen; 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a rowing eight is an oarsman pulling one of its oars.

clue.text: A short indication of approval heard for puzzle

indicators.note: heard says the words are said aloud and the sound is what is entered

parts.note: short means cross, irritable, and an indication of approval is a tick

explanation.surface: A brief sign of approval is overheard for a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' wants to shorten something, but it means curt, CROSS; many solvers try TIC as a short TICK.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which the initial letters of lines spell out a word.

clue.text: Turn of phrase used in papers on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: identity papers are ID
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A local expression appears in the newspapers of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is not literal.

clue.text: Wintry weather at present, after first sign of spring

indicators.note: the present-time word comes after the opening letter
the opening letter of spring is taken

parts.note: at present means now

explanation.surface: Cold weather has arrived just as spring shows its first sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is frozen flakes falling in cold weather.

clue.text: Garland given girl having tea at home

parts.note: Daisy is a girl's name
cha is slang for tea
in means at home

explanation.surface: A girl having tea at home is given a garland.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy chain is a string of daisies threaded together, worn as a garland.

clue.text: Accept members carry weapons

parts.note: to bear something is to accept or tolerate it
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Members of a group agree to be armed.
explanation.definitionFit: The right to bear arms is the right to carry weapons.

clue.text: Head, copping it, taken aback, is to serve a prison sentence

indicators.note: copping means catching or taking hold of, so the head word holds the other inside

parts.note: a dome is slang for the head

indicators.note: taken aback means turned backwards, so the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A headteacher, getting into trouble and shocked, is to be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copping it' reads as the British idiom for getting into trouble, but here 'copping' means catching hold of, and 'taken aback' turns the little word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing time is slang for being in jail serving a sentence.
